construction.note: Only the central rosette method is taken from Samira Mian. Most of the surrounding construction was worked out from @aslam.geometricpatterns’ finished drawing.
construction.changes: The construction is not a published step-by-step method for the whole Bou Inania panel. The shield band is omitted, joining shields to neighbouring dark pieces. The overlapping repeat and corner-star details were reconstructed, then simplified.

credits.creator: Samira Mian
credits.note: The rosette at the centre (inner circle from one chord, star lines joining its points 150° apart) follows her construction.

credits.source: Drawing of the Bou Inania pattern
credits.creator: @aslam.geometricpatterns
credits.note: Every line beyond the rosette was read from this drawing; the construction through crossings is our own reconstruction.

credits.source: Zellige of the Bou Inania madrasa, Fès (photograph, Wikimedia Commons)

given.A: Any point to the right of O. OA is the radius of the first circle.

steps.text: Draw a horizontal straight line through O and A. Draw a circle with centre O through A. Keep this compass size.

Draw circles with centres P0 and P180, through O. P0 is A, and P180 is where the line crosses the circle on the left. Draw a vertical line through O. It crosses the circle at P90 and P270. Draw circles with centres P90 and P270, through O.

The four new circles cross the first circle at P30, P60, P120, P150, P210, P240, P300 and P330. The circle is now cut into twelve. Draw a straight line through O and each of these points. Draw the lines through O that halve the angles between them. There is now a line through O every 15°.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: The four new circles cross the first circle at P30, P60, P120, P150, P210, P240, P300 and P330. The circle is now cut into twelve. Draw a straight line through O and each of these points. Draw the lines through O that halve the angles at 45°, 75° and 135°.

steps.text: Draw the line through O that halves the angle between the lines at 0° and 15°. Draw the line that halves the angle between 15° and 30°. These lines are at 7.5° and 22.5°.

Draw a straight line through P75 and P180. P75 is where the line at 75° crosses the circle. The line crosses the vertical line at T. Draw a circle with centre O through T. This is Samira Mian’s inner circle.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw a straight line through P75 and P180. P75 is where the line at 75° crosses the circle. The line crosses the vertical line at T. Draw a circle with centre O through T. This is Samira Mian’s inner circle.

steps.text: Join each of Q0 to Q330 to the point 150° round, with straight lines. Q0, Q30, Q60 and so on are where the inner circle crosses the lines through O at those angles. The twelve lines make the twelve-pointed star.

Draw circles with centres P0 and P30, the size of the first circle. They cross outside it at U, on the line at 15°. Draw a line through U, at 90° to the line from O through it. Turn this line round O. This makes the big twelve-sided figure.
Draw the ring of small stars and pentagons.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw the ring of small stars and pentagons.

parts.text: Draw a line through X1, at 90° to the line through O at 7.5°. X1 is where a star line crosses a side of the big figure. Draw its mirror image through X2. Turn both round O. These 24 lines make the small five-pointed stars.
Draw a line through P30, at 90° to the line from O to P30. It just touches the circle. Turn it round O. These are helper lines.
Draw a vertical line through X3, where the helper lines at P30 and P330 cross the horizontal line. Turn it round O. These lines close the pentagons.

steps.text: Draw the octagon of the corner stars, and the frame.

parts.text: Draw a line through X4, at 90° to the line through O at 22.5°. X4 is where a side of the big figure crosses one of the 24 lines. Turn it round O in eighths. This makes the octagon of the corner stars.
Draw a vertical line through X5, where an octagon side crosses one of the 24 lines. Turn it round O in quarters. This makes the frame and the edge of the tile.

steps.text: Draw the ring round the shields.

parts.text: Draw a vertical line through X6, where a star line crosses a pentagon line. Turn it round O. This is the inner side of the ring.
Draw a line through X7, at 90° to the line through O at 15°. X7 is where two of the 24 lines cross on the horizontal line. Turn it round O. These are the points of the ring.

steps.text: Draw the lines out into the corners.

parts.text: Draw a vertical line through X8, where a side of the big figure crosses the inner side of the ring. Turn it round O. These lines carry the star lines on into the corners.
Draw a line through X9, at 90° to the line through O at 45°. X9 is where the frame crosses a pentagon line. Turn it round O in quarters. These lines cross the corners.
Draw a line through X10, at 90° to the line through O at 15°. X10 is where a side of the big figure crosses a pentagon line. Turn it round O.
Draw a line through X11, at 90° to the line through O at 15°. X11 is where two of the 24 lines cross on the line at 45°. Turn it round O.

steps.text: Draw an eight-pointed star at each corner of the frame.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw an eight-pointed star at each corner of the frame.

parts.text: Draw a straight line through the other two corners of the little square between the big figure and the frame. It crosses the diagonal at Sa, the centre of the star.
Draw a horizontal line and a vertical line through Sa. They cross the line across the corner at two points of the diamond.
Draw a circle with centre Sa through one of these points. It crosses the horizontal and vertical lines again at the other two.
Join the four points with straight lines. This diamond and the little square make the eight-pointed star.

steps.text: Where the inner band breaks on the right or top side, draw a line across to the other side. The band breaks there too, because the next tile lies over it.
Join the centres of the four corner stars to mark the square tile that repeats. It holds the rosette, half the band on each side and a quarter star at each corner.

ink.text: Ink the twelve-pointed star and its petals, the ring of small stars and pentagons, and the ring round the shields. Ink the bands and corner stars out to the edge of the tile. Follow the faint grey ink, or tick “Also ink the copies round the centre”.

pattern.text: Put copies of the square side by side. The half bands of neighbouring tiles make whole bands. The quarters of four tiles make an eight-pointed star.
